reconciliation.summary: The Store now provides generic generation-bound lookup maps and atomic multi-object publication, and Forge uses the latter to publish a receipt plus terminal verifier result in one generation. Isolated generation measurements remain approximately linear in total history bytes: 148 bytes at one record, 1,264 at ten, 6,224 at fifty, 12,424 at one hundred, 31,024 at 250, and 62,024 at 500; the sampled commit remained filesystem-barrier dominated at about 14.6-20.8 ms. The residual is representation write amplification and the separate portable-WASM resource envelope, not a cross-backend value disagreement.

reconciliation.summary: The final integration path removes routine Forge semantic subprocesses and makes environment entry bounded. A nine-iteration micro-verifier benchmark reports setup 7.133 s in a fresh temporary project, verifier p50 2.156 s and p95/p99 2.817 s, and state-inspect p50 2.797 ms with p95/p99 47.734 ms; the first state sample is the projection establishment. In one measured verifier, provider work was about 31 ms, action publication 282 ms, and receipt-plus-result batch publication 998 ms, so Forge/Store orchestration was about 1.315 s. A controlled environment enter took 6.54 s cold while starting both residents and 0.25 s warm; its capsule is bounded and performs no repository-family enumeration. The remaining pressure is durable Store publication and first-fill artifact admission.
